generations.description: The original M3, built for homologation. Featured high-revving S14 inline-4 engine and exceptional handling. Iconic in motorsport and highly collectible.
First M3 with inline-6 engine (S50/S52). More refined and comfortable while maintaining performance. US model had different engine than European version.
Widely considered one of the best M3 generations. Featured S54 inline-6 engine producing 333 horsepower. Excellent balance of performance and daily usability.
First M3 with V8 engine (S65). Produced 414 horsepower with high-revving character. E92 coupe and E93 convertible variants. Last naturally aspirated M3.
First turbocharged M3 with S55 inline-6 engine producing 425 horsepower. Improved fuel economy and torque. M3 sedan and M4 coupe separated.
Latest M3 with S58 inline-6 engine producing 473-503 horsepower. Competition and CS variants available. More aggressive styling and advanced technology.
BMW's compact executive sedan with inline-6 engines. Featured excellent handling and build quality. Established 3 Series reputation for sporty luxury.
More refined 3 Series with improved technology. Featured updated inline-6 engines and better handling. Popular among enthusiasts for modification potential.
Widely considered one of the best 3 Series generations. Featured updated inline-6 engines and excellent handling. Balance of performance and daily usability.
3 Series sedan (E90), touring/wagon (E91), coupe (E92), convertible (E93). Turbocharged engines in 335i; 328i/330i with inline-6. Popular for modifications and daily driving.
Complete redesign with turbocharged engines standard. Featured improved fuel economy and technology. More refined while maintaining sporty character.
Latest 3 Series with improved technology and handling. Featured updated turbocharged engines and advanced safety features. More premium positioning.

First use of the 330i nameplate. The E46 330i introduced the M54B30 2.5L (later 3.0L) inline-6 engine producing 225-231 hp. Widely praised for balance of performance and usability. Popular for exhaust, intakes, suspension, and engine modifications.
330i with N52B30 inline-6 engine producing 255 hp. Available in sedan (E90), touring (E91), coupe (E92), convertible (E93). Popular platform for performance upgrades.
330i with turbocharged N20/N52 inline-4 or inline-6 engines. Complete redesign with improved fuel economy and technology. More refined while maintaining sporty character.
Latest 330i with turbocharged B46/B48 2.0L inline-4 engine producing 255 hp. CLAR platform with improved handling and technology. Available with mild-hybrid (eDrive).
M4 coupe and convertible with S55 inline-6 engine producing 425 horsepower. Separated from M3 sedan. Competition variant produced 444 horsepower.
Latest M4 with S58 inline-6 engine producing 473-503 horsepower. Competition and CSL variants available. More aggressive styling and advanced technology.
BMW's compact car with rear-wheel drive. Featured efficient engines and good handling. 135i variant with turbocharged inline-6 was a performance model.
Refined 1 Series with front-wheel drive introduced. Featured updated engines and improved technology. M135i variant offered high performance.
Latest 1 Series with front-wheel drive platform. Featured updated engines and improved technology. M135i variant with all-wheel drive available.
BMW's compact coupe and convertible with rear-wheel drive. Featured turbocharged engines and excellent handling. M2 variant was track-focused.
Latest 2 Series coupe with improved technology and handling. Featured updated turbocharged engines. M2 variant continued with high performance.
E28 5 Series (non-M); 528e, 533i, 535i.
E34 5 Series (non-M); 525i, 530i, 535i, 540i. Touring wagon available.
Widely considered one of the best 5 Series generations. Featured inline-6 and V8 engines. Excellent balance of luxury, performance, and build quality.
Controversial styling with improved technology. Featured updated engines and introduced iDrive. More modern but some preferred previous generation.
More refined design with improved technology. Featured turbocharged engines and better fuel economy. More comfortable and luxurious.
Latest 5 Series with improved technology and handling. Featured updated engines and advanced safety features. More premium and refined.
First generation M5. Hand-built with 3.5L inline-6 M88 engine derived from M1. Naturally aspirated, established M5 as the ultimate sport sedan.
Second generation M5 with updated 3.6L and later 3.8L inline-6 engines. Touring (wagon) variant introduced in limited numbers. Refined and more powerful than E28.
Widely considered one of the best M5 generations. Featured S62 V8 engine producing 394 horsepower. Perfect balance of luxury and performance.
M5 with S85 V10 engine producing 500 horsepower. High-revving character and exceptional performance. SMG transmission was controversial.
M5 with S63 twin-turbo V8 engine producing 560 horsepower. Improved torque and fuel economy. Competition variant produced 575 horsepower.
Sixth generation M5 with S63 twin-turbo V8 engine producing 600-617 horsepower. All-wheel drive standard. Competition and CS variants available.

Seventh generation M5 (G90 sedan, G99 Touring). S68 twin-turbo V8 plus electric motor plug-in hybrid producing 717 horsepower combined. xDrive all-wheel drive standard. First M5 Touring in the US market.
High-performance 3 Series variant with B58 turbocharged inline-6 engine producing 320 horsepower. Excellent balance of performance and daily usability.
Latest M340i with updated B58 engine producing 382 horsepower. Improved handling and technology. All-wheel drive available.
High-performance 3 Series with N54/N55 turbocharged inline-6 engine producing 300-320 horsepower. Popular for tuning potential and performance.
335i with N55 turbocharged inline-6 engine producing 300-320 horsepower. Improved fuel economy and technology. M Performance variants available.
3 Series with naturally aspirated inline-6 engines producing 230 horsepower. Good balance of performance and fuel economy. Popular daily driver.
328i with N20 turbocharged inline-4 engine producing 240 horsepower. Improved fuel economy and torque. More efficient than previous generation.
BMW's coupe, convertible, and Gran Coupe. Separated from 3 Series. Featured turbocharged engines and excellent handling. M4 was high-performance variant.
Latest 4 Series with updated styling and technology. Featured updated engines and improved handling. M4 continued as high-performance variant.
High-performance 4 Series variant with B58 turbocharged inline-6 engine producing 320-355 horsepower. Excellent balance of performance and luxury.
Latest M440i with updated B58 engine producing 382 horsepower. Improved handling and technology. All-wheel drive available.
High-performance 2 Series variant with B58 turbocharged inline-6 engine producing 335 horsepower. Excellent handling and driver engagement.
Latest M240i with updated B58 engine producing 382 horsepower. Improved handling and technology. All-wheel drive available.
BMW's compact M car with N55/S55 engines producing 365-405 horsepower. Track-focused with excellent handling. Competition and CS variants available.
Latest M2 with S58 inline-6 engine producing 453 horsepower. More powerful and aggressive styling. Competition variant available.
High-performance 1 Series coupe and convertible with N54/N55 turbocharged inline-6 engine producing 300-320 horsepower. Popular for tuning potential.
M135i with N55 turbocharged inline-6 engine producing 315-320 horsepower. Front-wheel drive platform but still offered good performance.
BMW's first supercar, developed in collaboration with Lamborghini. Mid-engined with M88/4 inline-6 engine producing 277-280 horsepower. Built for homologation and highly collectible.
Limited production high-performance 1 Series coupe. Twin-turbo N54 inline-6 producing 335-340 horsepower. Rear-wheel drive, 6-speed manual only. Only ~6,300 units produced globally.
First generation M6 (M635CSi). Featured M88/3 inline-6 engine related to M1, producing 286-340 horsepower depending on market. Naturally aspirated grand tourer.
Second generation M6 with S85 V10 engine shared with E60 M5. High-revving character. Available as coupe (E63) and convertible (E64). Modern return of M6 after long hiatus.
Third generation M6 with S63 twin-turbo V8 engine. Available as coupe (F13), convertible (F12), and Gran Coupe (F06). More power and modern technology. Replaced by M8 in 2019.
High-performance 8 Series with S63 twin-turbo V8 engine shared with F90 M5. Available as coupe (F92), convertible (F91), and Gran Coupe (F93). Competition variants available. Replaces M6.
M Roadster - high-performance roadster variant of Z3. Featured S50/S52/S54 inline-6 engines depending on market and year. Excellent handling and driver engagement.
M Coupe - fixed-roof variant with 'Clown Shoe' body style. More rigid than roadster. Featured S50/S52/S54 inline-6 engines. Highly sought after by enthusiasts.
First generation Z4 roadster and coupe. Featured inline-6 engines. E85 roadster and E86 coupe. Shared platform with Z4 M.
Second generation Z4 with retractable hardtop. Featured N20/N52/N54 engines. More refined than E85/E86.
Third generation Z4 roadster. Shares B58/S58 engines and platform with Toyota Supra. Popular for B58 tuning and shared aftermarket parts.
Z4 M Roadster (E85) and M Coupe (E86) with S54 inline-6 engine producing 330 horsepower. High-revving naturally aspirated engine. Excellent handling and driver engagement.
Limited production roadster with aluminum space frame. Featured S62 V8 engine producing 400 horsepower. 6-speed manual transmission. Only ~5,703 units produced. Highly collectible.
First generation X3 M with S58 twin-turbo inline-6 engine producing 473-503 horsepower. Competition variant standard for 2021+. xDrive all-wheel drive standard.
First generation X4 M coupe-SUV with S58 twin-turbo inline-6 engine producing 473-503 horsepower. Shares platform with F97 X3 M. Competition variant standard for 2021+.
First generation X5 M with S63 twin-turbo V8 engine producing 547 horsepower. Introduced M performance to SUV segment. All-wheel drive standard.
Second generation X5 M with updated S63 engine producing 575 horsepower. Improved styling and technology. Shares platform with F86 X6 M.
Third generation X5 M with Competition variant producing up to 616 horsepower. 2024 LCI update introduced mild-hybrid S68 V8. Standard X5 M dropped, Competition only.
First generation X6 M with S63 twin-turbo V8 engine producing 547-560 horsepower. Crossover coupe SUV with dramatic styling and strong performance.
Second generation X6 M with S63 engine producing 567 horsepower. Updated styling and technology. Shares platform with F85 X5 M.
Third generation X6 M producing 600-617 horsepower. Competition variants available. 2023 LCI update introduced mild-hybrid S68 V8. Improved power and efficiency.

First electrified M Original since M1. Plug-in hybrid with V8 + electric motor producing 644 horsepower. Label Red variant produces 738 horsepower, making it the most powerful production BMW M model. Standalone performance SUV.

Electric M Performance variant of i4 Gran Coupe. Dual-motor all-wheel drive producing 536 horsepower. 0-60 mph in 3.7 seconds. EPA range 227-269 miles. Features adaptive M suspension and M Sport Brakes.
Electric M Performance variant of i5 sedan. Dual-motor xDrive producing 593 horsepower and 586 lb-ft torque. 0-60 mph in 3.7 seconds. EPA range 240-256 miles. 84.3 kWh usable battery.

Electric M Performance variant of i7 flagship sedan. Dual-motor all-wheel drive producing 650 horsepower, up to 811 lb-ft torque with M Sport Boost. 0-60 mph in 3.5 seconds. EPA range ~295 miles. 101.7 kWh usable battery.

Electric M Performance variant of iX SUV. Dual-motor all-wheel drive producing 610 horsepower and 749 lb-ft torque. 0-60 mph in 3.6 seconds. EPA range ~285 miles. 109.5 kWh battery with fast DC charging.
First-gen X1, rear-wheel-drive compact SUV on E9x platform.
Second-gen X1 on UKL FWD-based platform; M35i variant with B48 engine.
Third-gen X1 on FAAR platform; iX1 EV variant.
First-gen X2 on UKL platform; M35i high-performance variant.
First-gen X3 on E46 3-Series platform.
Second-gen X3; N20/N52/N55 engines.
Third-gen X3 on CLAR platform; M40i variant with B58 engine.
First-gen X4 on X3 F25 platform.
Second-gen X4 on CLAR; M40i variant with B58 engine.
First-gen X5; V8 and inline-6 engines.
Second-gen X5 (non-M); includes 35d diesel and 50i V8 variants.
Third-gen X5; xDrive35i/35d/50i and M50d.
Fourth-gen X5 on CLAR; M60i with S68 V8.
First-gen X6 (non-M); shared E70 platform.
Second-gen X6 on F15 platform.
Third-gen X6 on CLAR; M60i variant.
First-gen X7; three-row SUV flagship. M60i and Alpina XB7 variants.
Four-door coupe on UKL FWD-based platform; M235i xDrive variant.
First-gen 6-Series grand tourer; 630CSi, 633CSi, 635CSi, L6 (non-M).
Second-gen 6-Series coupe (E63) / convertible (E64); 645Ci, 650i.
Third-gen 6-Series convertible (F12), coupe (F13), Gran Coupe (F06); 640i, 650i.
6-Series Gran Turismo five-door fastback; replaced 5-Series GT.
First-gen 7 Series; 733i, 735i, 745i Euro turbocharged.
Second-gen 7 Series; M30 straight-6 and M70 V12 (750iL).
Third-gen 7 Series; 740i, 740iL, 750iL V12.
Fourth-gen 7 Series; 745i/745Li, 750i/750Li, 760Li V12. First iDrive.
Fifth-gen 7 Series; twin-turbo N54/N55/N63 engines.
Sixth-gen 7 Series on CLAR; M760i V12 available.
Seventh-gen 7 Series (non-M70; non-i7 variants).
First-gen 8 Series grand tourer; 840Ci, 850i, 850Ci, 850CSi V12.
Second-gen 8 Series; convertible (G14), coupe (G15), Gran Coupe (G16). 840i, M850i.
First-gen i3 electric compact on LifeDrive CFRP chassis; range-extender variant available.
Electric Gran Coupe; eDrive35, eDrive40, xDrive40 variants (M50 is separate model).
Electric 5-Series; eDrive40 and xDrive40 (M60 is separate model).
Electric 7-Series; xDrive60 (M70 is separate model).
Z3 roadster (E36/7) / coupe (E36/8). 1.9L-3.0L I6. Base Z3 (Z3 M seeded separately).
